title: soft-launch-primer-and-client-escape-cribsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal primer for a controlled soft-launch of model flip / minor version rollout to a small set of customers + a compact escape/rollback cribsheet that product/platform can eyeball during busy deploy windows. Keep short — this is my running checklist and heuristics, not a formal runbook.

Scope:
- Target: hosted-api model v2.14 -> v2.15-lite (quantized) for lower cost on short-text workloads.
- Cohorts: 3 external client cohorts (alpha, beta, warmup) + internal e2e traffic.
- Goal: validate latency and quality within 72h, ensure <3% request error uplift and no >15% QoQ regression on anchor prompt set.

Quick TL;DR rollout plan:
1) Warmup (0h-4h): internal traffic only (service-account jobs + smoke clients). Check p95 latency and KV cache behavior.
2) Alpha (4h-12h): 0.5% production traffic carved from low-risk tenants (existing partners who agreed). Observe cost/unit and safety signals.
3) Beta (12h-24h): 2% traffic, add a second geo (EU). Soft A/B route with SDK pin for clients opted-in.
4) Ramp (24h-72h): step to 10% then 25% if green. Hold for at least 4 hours on each step.
5) Full flip: post 72h + signoff from SRE and product.

Warmup checks (must pass before moving to Alpha):
- p50/p90/p95 latency: baseline delta <= +10ms p50, +25ms p95 on same SLA class.
- Error rate: total 5xx + 4xx < 0.2% absolute increase vs baseline.
- Token cost: estimated token-cost drop aligns with bench (within +/-10%).
- Quality smoke: for 20 anchor prompts, similarity score >= 0.92 vs control (quick embedding cosine check).
- KV cache priming: heatmap shows top-50 prefixes with cache hit rate > 60% after warmup.

Alpha/Beta cohort selection notes:
- Prefer long-lived tenants with predictable low concurrency (so variance low). Avoid partners using heavy function-calling or complex tool chains in first cohorts.
- For EU beta, confirm no network egress surprises (double-check region routing config).

Traffic steering / pinning strategy:
- Use SDK runtime flag (client-side pin) for cohort assignment where possible. If not, route via per-tenant route-key on edge LB.
- Keep server-side fallback: requests specifying model v2.15-lite should fallback to v2.14 on any error code >= 500 or latency > 2s.
- TTL for rollouts: set cohort pin TTL = 12h to allow quick rebalancing.

Rollout metrics dashboard (what I'll watch):
- Error surface: 500s / 4xx by tenant, by model version.
- Latency buckets: p50/p90/p95/p99 token & request.
- Quality regression: anchor set pass rate + top-line customer-reported hallucination flags.
- Cost delta: tokens-per-response and GPU-utilization by instance group.
- Cache hit rate: prefix/KV hit % over time.
- Backpressure: queue depth on serving runtime and autoscaler reaction time.

Automatic fallback rules (configured in routing):
- If p95(latency_v2.15) > p95(latency_v2.14) + 200ms for 5m window -> programmatic divert to v2.14.
- If 5xx rate increases by > 0.5% absolute across any 5m window -> divert and notify.
- If client-anchored quality metric falls below threshold (see linked eval) -> divert + page on-call.

Manual abort / rollback triggers (raise page immediately):
- Severe customer-visible regressions (sustained incorrect behavior flagged by CS for >2 customers).
- Any data leakage or secrets misconfig.
- Sustained autoscaler thrash or instance crashes (>=3 instance restarts in 10m).

Escape hatch checklist (for quick human rollback):
- Endpoint switch (control plane): flip routing policy to prefer v2.14 (5 clicks + confirm).
- Client flag flush: revoke experimental SDK flags via feature-flag service.
- Scale up buffer nodes for v2.14 to soak traffic (increase reserved capacity by +20% for 30m).
- Re-direction webhook to stub/echo endpoint for triage (temporary response).
- Notify: #incidents, #prod-rollouts, CS leads, and product PM.
- Post-mortem owner assignment within 24h if rollback happened.

Observability instrumentation reminders (DO NOT forget):
- Add model_version tag to all traces and logs for cross-filtering.
- Ensure sampling rate high for error traces during alpha (set to 100% for 1h).
- Add short-lived eval job: run 200 anchor prompts every 30m and write to monitoring index.
- Trace propagation across gateway -> runtime -> infra for top 20 slowest requests.

Notes on canary size heuristics (quick heuristics I use):
- Start very small (0.5%) if tenant diversity unknown. For well-understood tenant cohorts, 2% alpha may be fine.
- Use multiple small cohorts vs one medium cohort for better signal isolation.

Draft messaging for CS + partners (short):
Subject: Heads-up: small soft-launch of model improvements (v2.15-lite)
Body: HI — over the next 72h we'll route a small % of your traffic to a lower-cost runtime variant to test latency and stability. You can opt-out by setting the client flag "model_pin=v2.14". If you see anything odd, please ping #prod-rollouts and CS.

Open questions / TODOs (my personal follow-ups):
- "similarity score" threshold: verify exact metric/embedding model to use (@Miguel to confirm).
- Confirm if billing dashboard will reflect per-tenant model variant costs within 24h (billing delay caveat).
- Confirm autoscaler soft-limit behavior for quantized instances (Kenji).
- Add a lightweight E2E test that simulates function call heavy requests (Priya).

Quick crib notes for on-call (pasteable):
- If latency spike: check p95 by model -> if v2.15 > v2.14 + 200ms, flip routing to v2.14 and re-run warmup.
- If increased 5xx: divert immediately and check instance logs for 'out-of-memory' or 'cuda driver error'.
- If quality regression: collect 20 failing prompts, upload to /evals/quick-v2.15 and tag "rollback-candidate".

Post-launch follow-ups (if launch completes):
- Run full eval suite at 24h/72h and compare to baseline.
- Cost analysis: tokens-per-response and GPU-hour delta; surface to finance for potential pricing tweaks.
- Consider graduated dequantization for heavy workloads if quality issues appear.

Notes to self (freeform):
- Keep default fallback aggressive for the first 48h. Easier to undo conservative than to recover from degraded customer experience.
- This variant is a risk-reward play: wins on cost but small risk on hallucination heuristics for context-rich prompts.
- Don't trust one metric alone; look for correlated signals (latency + error + quality).

References / quick links:
- warmup scripts: https://repo.redwood/warmup-scripts (internal)
- eval notebook: https://notebooks.redwood.com/evals/anchor-v2-compare
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2734
- Jira: JIRA-8142, JIRA-8196

-- end --

(If nothing else, carry this doc into the deploy channel as a compact checklist when I run the rollout.)
